domain: Constitutional Law / Dynastic Succession / Political History
topic_summary: Analysis of Salic Law as a contested kernel in European dynastic succession systems. The historical codified prohibition on female inheritance is read by agnatic dynasties as an immutable divine mandate versus read by sovereigns lacking male heirs as an archaic legal husk subject to sovereign override. This authority-grounding contest historically triggered major continental conflicts including the War of Austrian Succession.

key_entities: Salic Law (6th century Frankish legal code, Title 62 excluding females from land inheritance)
Agnatic dynasties (Bourbon Spain, Bourbon France pre-Revolution, various German principalities)
Habsburg Monarchy (Maria Theresa's succession via Pragmatic Sanction 1713)
Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 (Charles VI's decree reversing Salic precedent)
War of Austrian Succession 1740-1748 (military enforcement contest)
key_tensions: Immutability claim vs sovereign override authority (who has final interpretive power over succession law)
Divine right legitimation vs pragmatic dynastic continuity (theological vs practical authority grounding)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Salic Law Title 62: prohibition on female inheritance of royal domains, originally land law extended to crown succession
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between (1) custodial interpretation by established dynasties claiming divine/natural law grounds, (2) sovereign legislative power claiming authority to revise or suspend

readings.commitment: Salic Law as irrevocable natural/divine law embedded in dynastic constitution
readings.authority_grounding: theological-custodial: dynasty interprets immutable divine order
readings.expected_structural_delta: Female heirs categorically excluded from succession; challengers to female succession legitimate; preventive war justifiable to enforce agnatic priority

readings.commitment: Salic Law as revocable positive law subject to sovereign legislative authority
readings.authority_grounding: absolutist-legislative: reigning monarch's decree supersedes prior custom
readings.expected_structural_delta: Female succession permissible via sovereign act (Pragmatic Sanction); challengers are rebels against legitimate authority; defensive war to protect dynastic continuity

readings.commitment: Salic Law as Frankish anachronism never properly binding on non-Frankish territories
readings.authority_grounding: historicist-territorial: pre-Salic customs retain precedence in non-Frankish domains
readings.expected_structural_delta: Female succession via cognatic primogeniture (eldest child regardless of sex); Salic Law inapplicable outside original Frankish jurisdiction; territorial integrity privileged over agnatic purity

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single framework can hold both 'divine law is irrevocable by human authority' (immutable) and 'sovereign decree supersedes all prior law' (override). Accepting one axiom requires rejecting the other.

No single framework can hold both 'Salic prohibition is universally binding natural law' (immutable) and 'Salic Law was never legitimately extended beyond Frankish jurisdiction' (reversion). One claims universal binding force, the other denies it ever validly applied.
